config.training_prompt:
What's the best programing language for implementing the following coding problem? Output only the name of the programming language, nothing else. Do not include explanations or code or Markdown code fences.

{description}

interpretation: 200 problems held out from fine-tuning; the same fixed random subset of 10 selected the checkpoint. Before/after generation uses all 200 on each GPU. Correctness is Qwen3.8-27B judgment, not execution against tests

judged_trajectory.interpretation: Same fixed ten problems per GPU, generated and judged every 100 updates. Coding judgments do not select the checkpoint; C/Java first-assistant-token validation loss selects it and controls early stopping every 25 updates. Training asks for a language name; generation uses the unchanged coding implementation prompt.

judge_runtime_note: Judge runtime transition: Transformers BF16/eager batch one for ['baseline']; batched vLLM for ['selected', 'interval/step-000100', 'interval/step-000200', 'interval/step-000300', 'interval/step-000400', 'interval/step-000500', 'interval/step-000600', 'interval/step-000700', 'interval/step-000800', 'interval/step-000900']. The pinned full Qwen3.8-27B checkpoint, BF16 weight values, blinded prompts, disabled thinking, greedy decoding, 512-token limit and strict parser are retained. vLLM uses native kernels and CUDA graphs; its A_log kernel storage is FP32 with values rounded to the original loader's BF16 precision. Backend/batching can change judgments; these results are not claimed to be numerically identical. Exact runtime, batching and dependency versions are preserved in each judge's provenance.
